key_insight: Water adsorption and especially H2O dissociation on g-C3N4 nanosheets substantially improves optical absorbance and electronic conductance, supporting stronger photocatalytic water-splitting performance.
engineering_relevance: The results identify g-C3N4 surface chemistry as a tunable lever for designing more efficient, sunlight-driven hydrogen production materials.
method: DFT used to benchmark the nanosheet’s electronic/optical properties.
SCC-DFTB simulations examined the effects of adsorbed H2O and OH on photocatalytic parameters.
ReaxFF molecular dynamics modeled multi-molecule water emission and H2 evolution trends.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent computational evidence that dissociated water (HO and O species) yields higher absorbance and conductance than pristine g-C3N4.
watch_item: The conclusions are simulation-based, so experimental validation and sensitivity to surface defects, coverage, and environment remain important before deployment.
paper_title: Computational Study of Water Adsorption and Dissociative Mechanisms Impacting g-C3N4's Optical and Electronic Properties
